jobs.excerpt: Strategic Advisor, Change ManagementAdvisory | United States (Remote) | Full-Time | NAM Who We Are: Front Office Transformation Experts Bluprintx (BPX) is a global, AI-powered consultancy built to design and deliver the intelligent front office for CMO and CRO executives.
jobs.description:
Strategic Advisor, Change Management

Advisory | United States (Remote) | Full-Time | NAM

Who We Are: Front Office Transformation Experts

Bluprintx (BPX) is a global, AI-powered consultancy built to design and deliver the intelligent front office for CMO and CRO executives. We are private equity-backed and scaling fast, with 300 active customers across 10 countries and more than 1,750 implementations. We connect people, technology, and AI to turn fragmentation into performance, partnering with global leaders to modernize how marketing, CRM, content, AI & Data connect. At BPX, we hire operators and specialists who thrive at the intersection of commercial strategy and technical execution.

What We Do: Cutting Complexity Across the Front Office

We help the world's most ambitious companies, including Uber Eats, BNY, and Xerox, untangle the operational complexity that slows enterprise growth. As a Gold Adobe Solution Partner and Salesforce Summit Partner, we deliver strategy and implementation across the full front office. Our proprietary methodology builds sustainable enabled ecosystems that maximize ROI and accelerate speed to market. By embedding AI into commercial workflows, we help clients move faster and stay ahead.

The Role

You'll be the senior advisor our clients turn to when a transformation has to land with people, not just in platforms. The seat has two halves. First, you'll set change management strategy at enterprise level, working directly with C-suite and senior leaders to define how their organization moves to new ways of working across marketing, sales and service. Second, you'll run the change management programs inside our largest MarTech, CRM and data transformations, from impact assessment through to measured adoption in the months after go-live.

You'll work alongside other Senior Strategic Consultants, shaping each client's multi-year roadmap, our Solution Architects, who design the platform and integrations, and our Program Managers, who run delivery. You'll also help BPX grow, using change strategy as a lever to expand existing accounts and land new ones, and you'll shape how our change management capability develops across the global consulting team.

What you'll do

  • Set change management strategy for client organizations, aligning operating model, roles, governance and ways of working to the outcomes of a multi-year transformation roadmap.
  • Advise C-suite sponsors as a trusted, technology-agnostic voice, coaching executives on what their teams need from them at each stage and raising adoption risk early and plainly.
  • Run change programs on large MarTech transformations across Adobe, Salesforce, Braze and data platforms, owning the change workstream from impact assessment to sign-off.
  • Assess impact and readiness, mapping stakeholders, role and process changes and skills gaps, then holding go-live decisions to evidence that teams are ready.
  • Design communication, training and enablement plans for every audience, from frontline marketing and sales teams to senior leaders and centers of excellence.
  • Measure adoption and value after launch, defining the metrics, tracking usage in the live platforms and fixing what stalls early.
  • Lead workshops and design deliverables that give clients clear, practical guidance across people, process, data and technology.
  • Shape change in pre-sales, scoping approach, effort and commercial model when a transformation needs a dedicated change workstream, and spotting growth opportunities within existing accounts.
  • Build the BPX change practice, turning what works on each engagement into frameworks, templates and accelerators, and mentoring consultants across the global team.

What you'll bring

  • Ten or more years in strategy, transformation or change consulting, including several years leading change on enterprise CRM, MarTech or data programs.
  • Strategy and delivery range: a track record of both setting enterprise change strategy and running the programs that deliver it, across people, process, technology and data.
  • A proven change method such as Prosci ADKAR, ACMP standards or Kotter, applied on live client programs. Formal certification is an advantage.
  • Credibility at C-suite level, with evidence of building long-term advisory relationships and being the voice senior leaders trust when decisions get hard.
  • Large transformation experience in marketing, customer experience, digital or business transformation, working across multiple workstreams and senior governance.
  • Front office platform fluency across marketing automation, CRM, customer data platforms, journey orchestration and workflow tools, enough to know how they change someone's working day.
  • Comfort with adoption data: you define the metrics, read the dashboards and use them to decide what to fix.
  • Commercial instinct, with experience contributing to proposals, scoping and estimating work, and growing accounts through consultative selling.
  • Sector breadth across B2B and B2C. Experience in highly regulated industries such as financial services is a strong advantage.

Why this role, why now

Our clients are investing more than ever in their front office platforms, and the programs keep getting bigger. What decides whether that investment pays back is adoption, and that is where this seat sits. It's a new, senior role, so you'll set how BPX advises on change at the strategy table, how we run it on the ground, and the practice every program after yours will draw on.

Additional information

Location: Remote, United States.

Compensation: The anticipated base salary range for this role is

125,000–190,000 USD per year. Where you land in the range depends on your experience and skills.

Benefits: medical insurance, 401k, PTO, sick leave and remote working.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity or expression), religion, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or any other basis protected by local, state or federal law. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications and business need. We are committed to an accessible recruitment process and will consider requests for reasonable accommodation at any stage, contact us to discuss what you need.

jobs.description:
Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at .

What you’ll be part of:

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder.

What you'll be responsible for:

Own end-to-end accounting for revenue and partner arrangements, ensuring accurate recognition, timely close, and complete disclosures across customer and partner incentives. Maintain and improve internal controls and reporting, partner with commercial, legal, tax, and data teams to define accounting and control requirements, and support internal and external audits. Identify, design, and implement AI and automation solutions — including generative models such as ChatGPT and Gemini — to reduce manual work, improve quality, and preserve human oversight and audit readiness.

What you'll work on:


  • Own month end and quarter end close for revenue and partnership arrangements, including subledger reviews, journal entries, account reconciliations, investigation and resolution of reconciling items, and related controls.
  • Analyse balance sheet and P&L movements, investigate anomalies and provide clear, evidence based commentary on key drivers, including timely review and circulation of the revenue flash.
  • Partner with FinOps and Product teams on new and evolving products, proactively reviewing product documentation and transaction and fund flows to identify accounting implications and define accounting, data, system, control and reporting requirements ahead of launch.
  • Review customer and partner arrangements and apply ASC 606 and other relevant U.S. GAAP to complex or non standard terms, documenting conclusions in clear, audit ready accounting memos.
  • Review expected credit loss provisions and underlying assumptions, ensuring estimates are appropriately supported, documented and reflected in the financial statements.
  • Partner with FinOps, Product, Billing, Legal, Tax, Data and Engineering teams to translate accounting conclusions and requirements into scalable processes, systems, controls and reporting.
  • Own the accounting for customer and partner incentives, including understanding end-to-end process and data flows, validating incentive calculations against contractual terms and supporting data, and recording appropriate accruals, true-ups, and journal entries with clear documentation and controls.
  • Take end to end ownership of assigned areas, proactively resolving issues, maintaining high quality documentation and audit readiness, and identifying AI and automation opportunities that simplify processes, strengthen controls and reduce manual work while maintaining appropriate human judgement and governance.

What you'll bring to Circle:

Core requirements:

  • 4+ years of relevant accounting, revenue or audit experience with ACA, CPA, ACCA or equivalent professional accounting qualification.
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP and/or IFRS, particularly ASC 606 / IFRS 15, with hands-on experience applying revenue recognition guidance to complex and judgemental arrangements.
  • Strong technical accounting and problem solving skills, with the ability to understand new products and commercial arrangements, assess their accounting implications and translate conclusions into clear accounting and system requirements.
  • Strong systems and data mindset, with the ability to understand transaction and fund flows across systems, investigate complex datasets and identify and resolve process, data or accounting gaps.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare high quality accounting memos and explain complex accounting matters clearly to Finance and non Finance stakeholders.
  • High ownership, attention to detail and quality standards, with the ability to take end to end responsibility for accounting processes, controls and audit readiness with limited oversight.
  • Hands-on experience using AI, automation or data tools to solve problems and improve processes, with a strong drive to simplify and automate work while maintaining appropriate judgement, governance and controls.

Preferred requirements:

  • Experience in payments, crypto, banking or technology companies
  • Experience with Oracle fusion or other similar ERP systems and transaction subledgers (Oracle or similar)
  • Experience/familiarity with Slack, Apple MacOS and GSuite

For more than a century, Big Brothers Big Sisters has been helping change kids’ perspectives and giving them the opportunity to reach their potential.

Since 1904, Big Brothers Big Sisters has operated under the belief that inherent in every child is incredible potential. As the nation’s largest donor- and volunteer-supported mentoring network, Big Brothers Big Sisters makes meaningful, monitored matches between adult volunteers (“Bigs”) and children (“Littles”), ages 5 through young adulthood in communities across the country. We develop positive relationships that have a direct and lasting effect on the lives of young people.

Position Purpose

The Director of Strategic Philanthropy serves as a frontline fundraiser responsible for identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding a portfolio of major individual donors in support of Big Brothers Big Sisters of America's (BBBSA) mission and strategic priorities. Reporting to the VP, Strategic Philanthropy, this role builds meaningful, long-term relationships with donors capable of six and seven-figure gifts, translating BBBSA's impact and strategic priorities into compelling, donor-centered cases for support.

The Director of Strategic Philanthropy partners closely with the Resource Development team, program and agency leaders, and executive staff to develop personalized cultivation strategies, craft gift proposals, and ensure a high-quality donor experience across the giving lifecycle. The role plays a critical part in growing BBBSA's individual giving program and advancing its national fundraising goals.

The ideal candidate is a relationship-driven fundraiser with a track record of closing six and seven- figure gifts, sound judgment, and the ability to manage a dynamic portfolio of prospects and donors in a mission-driven, federated organization.

Location: Continental United States (100% Remote),
FSLA Status: Full time, Exempt
Travel: Approximately 30-35%, with occasional additional travel as needed.

Remote Work Location Requirement: This position is approved for remote work within the Continental United States only. Any permanent change to the geographic location of an employee’s remote work arrangement from the region identified at the time of hire must be reviewed and approved in advance by both the employee’s direct manager and Human Resources.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Portfolio Management

  • Manage a portfolio of approximately 100-150 major donors and prospects, with individual gift capacity typically ranging from $25,000 to $100,000+.
  • Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for each donor in the portfolio using a moves management framework.
  • Maintain an active pipeline of qualified prospects sufficient to meet annual revenue goals, tracking stage, next steps, and timing for each relationship.
  • Document all donor interactions, moves, and strategies in the CRM in a timely and accurate manner to ensure institutional knowledge is preserved and shared.

Prospect Identification & Qualification

  • Partner with the prospect research function to identify new major gift prospects through wealth screening, referrals, and relationship mapping.
  • Qualify prospects through discovery visits and calls, assessing capacity, affinity, and readiness for solicitation.
  • Collaborate with local BBBS agency leaders to identify and cultivate donors with connections to both the national office and local chapters.

Cultivation, Solicitation & Stewardship

  • Design and deliver personalized cultivation experiences, including donor visits, briefings, campus and program tours, and executive engagement opportunities.
  • Draft compelling, donor-centered gift proposals, briefing materials, and stewardship reports in partnership with the Marketing & Communications and Program teams.
  • Directly solicit major gifts, leading or supporting solicitation visits alongside executive leadership, board members, or volunteers as appropriate.
  • Ensure timely, accurate gift acknowledgment and develop meaningful stewardship touchpoints that build long-term donor loyalty and encourage renewed and increased giving.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with the Resource Development team to align major gift strategies with annual fundraising goals, campaign priorities, and organizational strategic plans.
  • Work with Marketing & Communications to ensure donor-facing materials reflect current brand standards and effectively communicate BBBSA's impact.
  • Collaborate with Program and Agency leaders to stay current on organizational impact, outcomes data, and stories that strengthen donor cases for support.
  • Support executive and board engagement in major donor cultivation and solicitation, including briefing preparation and follow-up coordination.

Reporting, Documentation and Continuous Improvement

  • Track and report progress against individual and team revenue goals, pipeline metrics, and activity benchmarks on a regular cadence.
  • Maintain organized donor files and documentation utilizing the CRM, SharePoint, and other enterprise platforms.
  • Recommend improvements to major gift processes, tools, and donor journey design based on portfolio experience and outcomes.
  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives supporting the Resource Development team's effectiveness.
  • Manage related and other duties as assigned in support of department and business needs.

Culture

  • Demonstrate commitment to BBBSA's shared leadership competencies and organizational values.
  • Represent BBBSA's mission and impact with authenticity and donor-centered communication in every interaction.
  • Provide consistent follow-up regarding assigned donors and after meetings.
  • Cultivate an environment where colleagues, donors, and program partners feel valued, included, and heard.

Education, Skills & Related Work Experience

  • Education Level: Bachelor's degree or equivalent combinations of education and progressively responsible fundraising experience.
  • Years and Scope of Related Work Experience: Minimum of Five years of progressively responsible major gifts or frontline fundraising experience, with a demonstrated track record of identifying, cultivating, and closing five- and six-figure gifts. Experience managing a donor portfolio and moves management process required. Experience with Salesforce preferred. Experience within a nonprofit or federated organization preferred.

At Big Brothers Big Sisters of America, we recognize, affirm, and celebrate the backgrounds, lives, and experiences of all of our stakeholders, including youth, families, donors, volunteers, and staff. jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Spain Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-110,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Position Title

Capital Planning & Stress Testing Program Manager

Location

Nationwide, MI 48098

Job Summary

The Capital Planning & Stress Testing Program Manager leads Flagstar’s stress testing and capital planning processes, reporting to the Director of Capital Planning & Stress Testing. This role coordinates cross-functional teams to execute stress test plans, ensure regulatory compliance, and align with capital management policies. Responsibilities include developing and integrating stress testing processes, overseeing documentation, guiding scenario design, and preparing reports for senior management and regulators. The manager ensures that capital planning is effective, meets governance standards, and supports strategic decisions. This role exists to ensure the bank’s capital planning exercises are executed efficiently, meet regulatory expectations, and support sound strategic decision-making.

Job Responsibilities:

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Program Leadership & Plan Coordination: Leads the bank’s stress testing program, coordinating input from multiple departments to collect and integrate all necessary data and materials. Maintains and updates key capital planning documents (e.g., capital plan narrative, policies, contingency plans) to ensure the stress testing process is cohesive and aligned with business objectives.
  • Scenario Design & Challenge Oversight: Leads internal stress test scenarios informed by the bank’s idiosyncratic risks (Risk ID inventory) and evaluates capital adequacy under adverse conditions. Manages review/challenge sessions on forecasted results (e.g., PPNR, credit losses), addressing key assumptions and limitations through sensitivity analysis and appropriate overlays.
  • Reporting & Regulatory Submission: Prepares and submits regulatory stress testing reports and the final capital plan document, ensuring accuracy and timeliness. Produces clear summaries of stress test results and recommended capital actions for senior management and Board review and performs ad-hoc capital analyses (such as peer comparisons) to support decision-making.
  • Quality Assurance & Compliance: Ensures the consistency and reliability of stress test results through strong quality controls and data governance. Maintains an inventory of critical capital planning data elements, working with Data Governance to resolve data issues, and verifies adherence to internal risk management standards. Supports and addresses any findings from regulatory, risk, or internal audits and ensures continuous compliance with all relevant policies and regulatory requirements throughout the stress testing cycle.
  • Proactively manage examination requests, company resources, program risks, and required deliverables, as well as the day-to-day planning and resource allocation.
  • Responsible for talent management functions including: employment, performance evaluations, staff development/training, disciplinary actions, succession planning and ensuring all staff comply with compliance requirements.

ADDITIONAL ACCOUNTABILITIES

  • Strategic Alignment: Works under the direction of the CPST Director to ensure that stress testing activities support the bank’s strategic goals for capital adequacy and risk management. Provides input to senior leadership on opportunities to improve capital efficiency or risk mitigation based on stress test insights.
  • Governance and Policy Adherence: Upholds the governance framework for capital planning. Ensures that all activities follow the approved Capital Planning & Stress Testing policies and the governance standards set by management committees (CMC, ERMC) and the Board. All documentation and processes should withstand regulatory scrutiny and internal audit standards.
  • Continuous Improvement: Stays current on evolving regulatory expectations (e.g., Federal Reserve guidance for Category IV banks, Basel capital standards) and industry best practices in stress testing. Recommends and implements enhancements to the stress testing program, such as process improvements, model updates (in partnership with model development teams), and improved coordination mechanisms, to continually strengthen Flagstar’s capital planning capabilities.
  • Performs special projects, and additional duties and responsibilities as required.
  • Consistently adheres to regulatory and compliance policies and standards linked to the job as listed and complete required compliance trainings. Accountable to maintain compliance with applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Required Qualifications:

  • Education level required: Undergraduate Degree (4 years or equivalent) in Finance, Economics, Business, Mathematics or a related field (or equivalent work experience in a related discipline).
  • Minimum experience required: 6+ Years experience in financial risk management, capital planning, or stress testing. Involvement in enterprise stress testing processes or regulatory capital plan preparation.
  • Technical Skills: Knowledge of regulatory capital requirements and stress testing frameworks (e.g., DFAST/CCAR, Basel III). Proficiency in financial modeling and scenario analysis; advanced Excel skills.
  • Leadership & Communication: Proven ability to lead cross-functional projects or teams. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial analyses to senior executives. Collaborative team player who can influence and coordinate stakeholders across departments.
  • Analytical & Detail-Oriented: High attention to detail and accuracy. Strong analytical problem-solving skills to interpret model results and identify trends or issues. Effective at managing multiple priorities and deadlines, especially during peak stress testing cycles.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Education level preferred: Master's Degree (or Postgraduate equivalent) in Finance, Business Administration (MBA), Economics, or a related field or professional certification (CFA, FRM).
  • Experience working at a bank subject to regulatory stress testing (e.g., DFAST/CCAR submissions) and dealing with regulatory examinations.
  • Familiarity with data governance and model risk management practices related to capital planning. Exposure to liquidity risk or resolution planning.
  • Familiarity with data analysis tools or statistical modeling.

Job Competencies:

  • Regulatory Acumen: Understanding of capital planning regulations and expectations. Able to ensure the stress testing program meets regulatory standards.
  • Project Management: Organized and able to develop timelines, delegate tasks, and drive projects to completion on schedule.
  • Collaboration: Effective at building relationships and coordinating with various teams to gather information and achieve consensus.
  • Adaptability: Comfortable working under tight deadlines and changing requirements; remains calm and flexible during high-pressure periods.
  • Integrity: Maintains confidentiality of sensitive information and upholds high ethical standards. Ensures all activities comply with company policies and regulatory guidelines.
  • Demonstrates a strong ability to build and maintain effective relationships with stakeholders by communicating clearly, engaging in proactive collaboration, and leveraging cross functional insights. Aligns relationship building efforts with enterprise goals to accelerate performance and drive strategic results.
  • Builds trusted client relationships, whether internal or external, by identifying needs and delivering tailored solutions to enhance the overall client experience.
  • Fosters a positive work culture and productive work environment, driving strategy and displaying importance of effective relationships with customers and stakeholders to influence and coach.

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Poland Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-110,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

As part of the Sales Team, this is done primarily by running effective outbound campaigns, delivering strong discovery and sales calls over Zoom/Google Meet, actively listening and responding to challenging questions, and representing Hustler Marketing in the most beneficial way. This is a multi-functional position that requires you to source, qualify, and prepare future clients for our company, then carry them through the sales conversation yourself.

This role involves playing an active, hands-on part in the full sales process and having a thorough understanding of the services we offer. The Sales Development Representative position requires strong sales skills, high levels of creativity, comfort with data, and a genuine fluency with modern outbound tooling and AI. You will be expected to use AI for efficiency and automation wherever it makes the work faster and better, and to operate autonomously the majority of the time. In addition, the Sales Development Representative must be structured, efficient, and approachable, with excellent interpersonal skills, especially in a remote work environment.

The Sales Development Representative will report directly to the Vice President and Managing Director and be the liaison between prospective new clients and our internal teams at Hustler Marketing.

The primary mission of our Sales Development Representative is to be the front face of Hustler Marketing and to keep our sales pipeline consistently full of well-qualified, self-sourced leads. This includes owning the activities across our sales process, running discovery and sales calls, and working hard to ensure that our sales and onboarding processes are of the highest quality for our existing and future clients. You will be responsible for representing our company and our services to potential clients, especially highlighting Hustler Marketing in a positive and beneficial way, and for continuously finding ways to make the whole outbound engine leaner and more effective through better process and smart use of AI.

General Responsibilities:

  • Building and owning your outbound pipeline by contacting potential new clients through a variety of channels, including cold email, LinkedIn, cold calls, and other messaging and communication platforms
  • Running discovery and sales calls over Zoom/Google Meet with new and prospective clients, from first conversation through to close
  • Selling Hustler Marketing's digital agency services primarily to DTC brands, tailoring the pitch to each prospect's situation and goals
  • Researching and qualifying prospects to determine whether they fit our description of an ideal client and whether they will be a good fit for Hustler Marketing
  • Proactively seeking out new business opportunities within our target DTC market, and identifying adjacent segments worth pursuing
  • Fully owning and managing our Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform, keeping records clean, accurate, and up to date at all times, and providing clear progress reporting to the Vice President and Managing Director

jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

jobs.description:
About Opportunity@Work:

Opportunity@Work is a national nonprofit whose mission is to rewire the labor market so that STARs, workers who are skilled through alternative routes instead of a bachelor’s degree, can work, learn, and earn to their full potential. By 2030, Opportunity@Work aims to enable at least 1 million working adults in America to get hired into middle- and high-wage jobs, thus generating a $20 billion boost in annual earnings.

We are driven by a firm belief that “if you can do the job, you can get the job.” STARs earn valuable skills through pathways like military service, community college, talent development programs, partial college completion, or on-the-job experience, instead of through a bachelor’s degree. STARs are half of the U.S. workforce, yet over the last few decades they’ve been blocked from accessing millions of good-paying jobs – and have actually seen their wages decline.

Opportunity@Work’s research capabilities inform the nation’s understanding of STARs and uncover insights that show how to make positive change within regions and industries. Our national awareness campaign, “Tear the Paper Ceiling,” communicates a new, positive narrative about STARs and elevates contributions to the skills-first movement. We’ve developed accessible STAR-centric tools, powered by our data and generative AI, to help organizations make more informed decisions on inclusive workforce strategies and hiring.

#YouWantToBeHere

Position Summary:

As Director of Resource Mobilization, you will grow Opportunity@Work's philanthropic revenue by building relationships with institutional funders capable of investing $500K or more. You'll own a portfolio of current and prospective private and corporate foundations, moving each from cultivation to close and partnering with the Vice President and other executives on top-tier asks. A key part of the role is securing and/or enhancing the multi-year anchor partnerships that sustain our largest bodies of work. You'll represent Opportunity@Work with funders and philanthropic leaders, and work across teams to translate organizational priorities into compelling investment opportunities.

If you are a relationship-driven fundraising leader who is energized by opening doors, building new institutional partnerships, and turning shared interest into significant investment, we want to hear from you!

Key Responsibilities:

Funder Cultivation and Stewardship (75%)

  • Own a portfolio of current and prospective institutional funders, moving each from cultivation through solicitation and close, with a focus on securing new $500K+ investments and multi-year anchor partnerships.
  • Lead funder meetings and solicitations, connecting Opportunity@Work's mission and funding priorities to each funder's goals.
  • Design and carry out stewardship strategies that retain current funders and grow their investment year over year.
  • Identify and qualify new prospects, using workforce and philanthropic trends to decide where to focus.
  • Build and activate a network of philanthropic champions: well-connected leaders who may not fund us directly but can open doors, make introductions, and advocate for Opportunity@Work in rooms we aren't in.
  • Represent Opportunity@Work at conferences, convenings, and events to expand our funder network and influence.

Fundraising Strategy and Internal Partnership (25%)

  • Partner with the Executive Office to understand, capture, and build on the CEO's funder relationships and meetings, including preparing briefings and follow-up plans for CEO and executive engagement.
  • Work with the Senior Manager, Revenue Operations to keep Salesforce accurate across funders, prospects, champions, and events, and use that data to shape funder strategy and prioritization.
  • Partner with the Senior Manager, Resource Mobilization to develop proposals, presentations, and reports for portfolio funders that align with organizational goals and core messaging.
  • Serve as a liaison between Resource Mobilization and teams across the organization (Marketing, External Affairs, Programs, Finance, and others) so funding asks reflect organizational priorities, and we can deliver on what we commit to funders.
  • Serve as a role model across the organization, helping build a collaborative, fun, and results-oriented culture.

Qualifications and Core Competencies

  • 7+ years of nonprofit fundraising experience, including closing multiple $500K+ gifts from foundations or corporations.
  • A natural relationship-builder who can command a room and inspire confidence in funders and partners.
  • A strategic thinker who can structure fundraising problems, use data, and propose solutions to hit revenue targets.
  • Excellent collaboration skills, with a track record of aligning senior leaders and cross-functional teams around shared fundraising goals.
  • Exceptional writing and speaking skills, with the ability to craft narratives that resonate with diverse audiences.
  • Highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple funder relationships and deadlines at once.
  • Experience using Salesforce or a similar CRM to track engagement and pipeline.
  • Comfort and experience using AI tools.
  • Familiarity with workforce development, economic mobility, or systems-change philanthropy is a plus.
  • Embody our core values: better together, intentionally inclusive, always learning, seeking clarity to inform action, and championing empowerment.
  • A well-developed sense of humor and adaptability to change.

Opportunity@Work is an equal opportunity and skills-first employer. We celebrate diversity and the dignity of every worker - especially those with overlooked skills. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

  • Compensation:
    $116,063.00 - $140,000
  • Travel Requirements: As needed for key funder meetings/events (20%)

Please submit a thoughtful cover letter and resume to Opportunity@Work’s career page. We will review applications on a rolling basis and contact you if we move forward with a phone interview.

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Poland Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-110,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Italy Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-80,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

jobs.description:
Senior Support Engineer

Town Web · HeyGov · ClerkMinutes. Remote, Central US hours. $85,000 to $105,000 a year. Open to candidates in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland.

About us

We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government clients in almost every state in the U.S.

Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.

The role

This is the senior seat on our Client Success team. We are hiring you to raise the standard of our support: fix what is broken, write down how it should work, and show what great looks like.

Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.

This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.

It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem on the events calendar on the client's homepage, or in the calendar widget embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name only in the transcript, or is it also in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.

You need both halves. A brilliant troubleshooter who is short with a clerk will not work here. Neither will a lovely person who forwards every problem to a developer.

Your first 90 days

  • Learn all of our products well enough to teach them
  • Take over every open escalation and close or schedule each one
  • Rebuild the path from support to our developers so nothing leaves the queue untracked
  • Find the ten questions clerks ask most and fix each at the source: an article, a Fin answer, or a product change

What you will do

Raise the standard

  • Design how issues move from support to developers, and keep that path working
  • Set the bar for replies, calls, and write-ups, and coach teammates by example
  • Turn what you fix into playbooks the team and Fin can follow

Delight clients

  • Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
  • Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
  • Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
  • Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates

Own the problem from start to finish

  • Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
  • Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
  • Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue

Diagnose, then escalate

  • Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer
  • Reproduce it, capture the steps with screenshots or a recording, and file it in Linear with everything a developer needs
  • Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client
  • Use Claude, connected to our code repository, to trace where a behavior comes from. For small, well-understood fixes, draft the change for a developer to review

Knowledge base and AI support

  • Inherit and maintain the help center for all of our products. It is what our AI agent (Fin, in Intercom) answers from
  • Write and improve articles from real, recurring questions, on a weekly rhythm measured against live ticket volume
  • Write troubleshooting guides that separate look-alike problems, so the next person, or Fin, can tell them apart
  • Tune Fin: review where it failed, fix the article, and teach it to ask a clarifying question when a request could mean two things
  • Record short training videos so clients can learn at their own pace

Support and onboarding

  • Handle the conversations Fin cannot resolve across Town Web (websites), HeyGov (forms, payments, reservations, campaigns), and ClerkMinutes (agendas, transcripts, minutes)
  • Help new clients through onboarding with the projects team so they reach value quickly
  • Talk with clerks by phone and video every week. Get on a call whenever a situation needs a human voice

Account care

  • Build real relationships with your assigned accounts
  • Understand what each client is trying to accomplish, what they use, what they do not know we offer, and where they will need help before they ask
  • Run proactive, recurring check-ins instead of waiting for tickets. For example, reach out a few weeks after go-live to review how their forms are performing
  • Use product usage data to spot clients who are not getting full value yet
  • Meet clients in person. Join us at clerk conferences and marketing events a few times a year. We cover all travel & lodging expenses

Spot opportunity

  • Tell clients about services they do not use yet (digital forms, payments, .gov domains, accessibility, training) without it feeling like a pitch
  • Flag possible expansion and renewal opportunities to the sales team

Training

  • Get clients to real proficiency with the product, not just past their immediate question
  • Work with Product Managers to co-host webinars about new features and training

Tools you will use: Intercom and Fin, Linear, Claude, our help center, screen recording, Zoom phone.

How we work

  • Delight over deflection. The goal is happy, successful clients, not fewer conversations
  • Ownership over routing. A hard case is yours until it is resolved
  • Diagnose before you escalate. A developer should never have to ask what the client actually saw
  • Documentation is the foundation everything else runs on, not an afterthought
  • Teaching over ticket-closing. Proficiency, not just an answer

Who you are

  • You like people, and it shows. Clerks are often not technical, sometimes stressed, and now and then upset. You pick up the phone gladly and leave them calmer than you found them
  • Hospitable by nature. A background in hospitality or another service-first field is a plus
  • You have done support somewhere known for it. The standard we have in mind is Basecamp: competent, calm, and trusted to make the call
  • Technically deep. You read the error, open the browser console and the network tab, check a DNS record, find your way around WordPress, and follow the trail into the code with Claude's help
  • At home with developers. You know what a good bug report contains and you have filed plenty
  • High autonomy. You decide, act, and report. You do not wait to be told
  • A clear, warm, precise writer, with clients and across teams
  • A natural teacher, patient with less technical users
  • Able to see the whole account, not just the ticket in front of you

Who you might be

  • Someone who worked the Genius Bar at an Apple Store and misses solving problems for a person, not a queue
  • Someone who learned support at a company known for it, such as Basecamp, Automattic, or Help Scout
  • A hotel or hospitality professional who moved into software and kept the instincts
  • A former municipal or deputy clerk who was always the one who figured out the software. You already know our clients' world
  • Or maybe none of these! If the rest of this page sounds like you, we certainly want to hear from you

This is not the job for you if

  • You would rather work a queue than talk to people
  • You find non-technical users frustrating
  • You want to hand a problem to a developer and move on
  • You need someone to tell you what to do next

Work style

  • Independent and ownership-driven. You do not need heavy oversight to perform
  • Comfortable wearing several hats across products and brands
  • Comfortable in a lean, documentation-first team
  • Proactive rather than reactive with accounts

What success looks like

  • Clients describe working with us as a great experience
  • No client has to ask who is handling their problem. They already know it is you
  • Issues you file get fixed without a developer asking for more detail
  • Tickets stop recurring, not just get answered
  • Help center articles created or improved every week, and Fin resolving more each month
  • Repeat questions turned into product fixes or automation
  • Expansion and renewals tied to the accounts you touch
  • Account relationships that are trusted, not just responsive
  • The rest of the team gets better because you are on it

Requirements

Experience

  • Five or more years in technical support or support engineering at a software company, working directly with engineers
  • An issue tracker used daily: Linear preferred, Jira or similar is fine
  • Intercom or similar support tooling, including work with an AI support agent
  • A knowledge base you wrote that other people relied on
  • AI tools such as Claude already part of your daily work
  • Nice to have: government or municipal software, WordPress-based websites, hospitality or other service-first work
  • Able to travel within the US a few times a year. Not required, but very helpful to understand our customers better.

How to apply

  1. Apply through Workable. You will answer two short questions in writing and record a two-minute Loom video teaching us one thing
  2. Complete the Culture Index survey. You can do it right after you apply. We only review candidates who have completed it
  3. Interview with our Head of Client Success
  4. Paid take-home exercise built from real client situations
  5. Conversation with our CTO and founder, including a short role-play call with a clerk who needs help
  6. Offer letter, if selected

Benefits

  • Salary of $85,000 to $105,000 a year, depending on experience
  • 20 paid vacation days, plus public holidays for your country of residence
  • Fully remote, working Central US hours
  • Internet stipend
  • Gym membership or wellness stipend

We do not offer a health plan or a 401(k) today. The salary range reflects that.

As a member of a highly collaborative team, you will provide scientific leadership, support talent development, foster client partnerships, and help ensure operational excellence across a diverse portfolio of programs and accounts.

The Associate Medical Director operates as a player-coach, balancing scientific leadership responsibilities with hands-on involvement to support successful client outcomes, team development, and business growth.

  • Lead, mentor, and develop Medical Directors, Scientific Directors, and medical writers, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and professional growth.
