jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Louisville, KY, USA
jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

  • Підготовка ТЗ на проєктування

  • Розрахунок генерації
  • Участь в робочих нарадах, як внутрішніх так і з замовником
  • Погодження проєктів з представниками технічної служби замовника та/або з експертизою
  • Ведення авторського нагляду за реалізацією проєкту

  • Досвід роботи інженером-проектувальником

    - PVSyst для формування звітів, зокрема з погодинної генерації (є перевагою)
    - SketchUp для привязки геолокації, формування затінень, створення анімації (є перевагою)
    - Плагін Skelion для розкладання фотомодулів, розрахунку генерації, створення моделей власних ФЕМ (є перевагою)

  • Розрахунок втрат напруги та підбір перерізу кабелів
  • Знання типів кріплень ФЕМ до покрівлі (розуміння вузлів)

  • Досвід роботи з різними типами сонячного обладнання: знання складових СЕС, вимог та стандартів, щодо їх встановлення, підключення та експлуатації

Є додатковою перевагою:

  • Наявність сертифіката проектувальника СС1-СС3
  • Наявність сертифікатів від виробників обладнання про знайомство з характеристиками їх обладнання
  • Знання англійської мови (для ознайомлення з технічною документацією)

Ми пропонуємо:

Ця посада є гарною кар'єрною можливістю для фахівців, які прагнуть стати провідними експертами з проектування в одній з найдинамічніших компаній галузі.

jobs.title: Global Health Advisory - Engagement Manager
jobs.excerpt: Our Vision:We believe in a world where everyone, regardless of their country’s wealth or frontiers, enjoys access to medicines and healthcare when they need it.
jobs.description:
Our Vision:

We believe in a world where everyone, regardless of their country’s wealth or frontiers, enjoys access to medicines and healthcare when they need it.

Our Mission:

We work tirelessly to remove access barriers faced by patients and caregivers across Low and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs) when seeking quality medicines and quality healthcare.

Who We Are: Accelerating access to medicines for all

Imagine a world where critical medicines are within reach, affordable, and synonymous with quality, no matter where you are. That is the world we're building with our unique, demand-aggregation model that unites healthcare providers across LMICs. At the heart of our identity is a single, resolute commitment: to build a future where geography and income never stand between any individual and life-saving medicines. Our platform isn't merely a space for transactions, we unlock affordable access to medicines by aggregating demand across healthcare providers. We also help manufacturers build a sustainable and reliable global access strategy.

Our business focuses on low- and middle-income countries and strengthens the purchasing power of these markets to ensure the supply of cost-effective, high-quality medicines. We partner exclusively with authorized, high-quality pharmaceutical companies and certified caregivers to accelerate sustainable access to medicines.

Axmed Global Health Advisory is the access-focused advisory arm of Axmed, a social impact company dedicated to improving access to medicines across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). As a specialized advisory firm, Axmed Global Health Advisory partners with private sector, global health organizations, and industry stakeholders to develop and implement market access strategies, innovative financing models, and go-to-market solutions tailored to LMIC healthcare systems.

Please note: We're building our Global Health Advisory team ahead of exciting new engagements in 2027, so our hiring timeline for this role may be longer than usual. We'll keep you updated as things progress.

About the Position

As our Global Health Advisory continues to expand its portfolio of partners, we are seeking a detail-oriented and driven Global Health Advisory Engagement Manager to join our Advisory team. This role is central in supporting complex partner programs and advancing strategic initiatives that improve access to medicines in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs). The successful candidate will thrive in a start-up setting, bring a passion for expanding access to medicines in LMICs, and enjoy an advisory-style role that spans diverse projects from strategic analyses to client-facing program management.

This is a broad role combining analytical rigor with project management and stakeholder engagement. You will help run client-facing program management offices (PMOs), conduct market and landscape assessments, and contribute to the development of value propositions, go-to-market strategies, and innovative solutions. All of this work will be grounded in the realities and opportunities of LMIC health systems.

We value expertise or interest in the following domains:

  • Geography & market focus: understanding LMIC regional healthcare contexts and opportunities for access.

  • Portfolio strategy:analyzing assets for impact, prioritization, and relevance to LMIC patient needs.

  • Financing & pricing: exploring sustainable and innovative financing approaches for resource-constrained settings.

  • Channel & delivery models: assessing and designing pathways to reach patients effectively in LMIC contexts.

  • Partnerships & ecosystem engagement: working with diverse stakeholders (ministries of health, NGOs, funders, and private sector actors) to unlock access.

  • Go-to-market strategy: shaping strategies that connect products and patients in LMICs.

Above all, we are looking for someone who takes ownership, communicates with clarity, delivers high-quality outputs consistently, and proactively seeks solutions to challenges. You will join a lean team of specialists with roles ranging from analyst to principal, guided by a partner.

Key Responsibilities:

Project & Program Management

  • Support the planning, coordination, and execution of complex, multi-stakeholder programs for global health clients (including serving as part of client-facing PMO structures).

  • Drive high-quality preparation of deliverables, meeting materials, and reports, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and alignment with client needs.

  • Monitor progress against objectives, flag risks early, and propose practical solutions.

Strategic Analyses & Insights:

  • Conduct LMIC market and landscape analyses across geographies to assess opportunities, challenges, and competitive positioning.

  • Support portfolio and product strategy work to guide decision-making on where and how to play.

  • Develop value propositions and go-to-market strategies tailored to LMIC contexts, integrating evidence, stakeholder perspectives, and financing considerations.

  • Prepare presentations and reports to meet the clients' agreed deliverables and facilitate the clients’ execution of such strategy

Client & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with key clients, acting as their primary point of contact to ensure client satisfaction and long-term partnership growth.

  • Serve as a trusted partner to clients, supporting workshops, strategy sessions, and ongoing advisory interactions.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with diverse LMIC stakeholders (manufacturers, payers, policymakers, NGOs, and implementing partners).

  • Represent the team professionally in external engagements, ensuring communications are clear, concise, and solution-oriented.

Requirements:

  • A BS/BA degree in Public Health, Pharmacy, Life Sciences, Business, or a related field.

  • A Master's degree in a similar field will be preferred.

  • 5+ years of professional experience with significant exposure to LMIC healthcare settings, ideally in consulting, global health, or life sciences, with demonstrated project management and analytical skills.

  • Exposure to global health healthcare sectors like vaccines, essential medicines, diagnostics, health system strengthening, or health financing is a plus.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment, balancing analytical tasks with client-facing responsibilities.

  • Strong skills in research, analysis, and synthesis. Candidate needs to be able to transform complex information into actionable insights.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with experience engaging senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

What is in it for you?

At Axmed, we believe in creating a supportive and rewarding environment where our team can thrive. Here’s what we offer:

  • Unlimited PTO: Take the time you need to recharge and maintain work-life balance.

  • Monthly wellness allowance: Prioritize your health and well-being with extra support.

  • Paid parental leave: Time off to bond with your new family member without any added stress.

  • Flexible working hours: Enjoy the freedom to structure your workday in a way that suits your lifestyle.

  • Annual off-site retreats: Connect with the team and build lasting relationships during our company retreats.

  • Fully remote work: Work from anywhere in the world and join our distributed team.

  • The opportunity to make a difference: Be part of a mission-driven company working to improve healthcare equity.

  • Competitive salaries: We offer a compensation package that reflects your skills and experience.

  • Plenty of room for growth: We believe in nurturing talent and offering opportunities for professional development and advancement.

Work at Home Bilingual Pohnpeian-English Phone Interpreter

Job Title: Pohnpeian Interpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Phone Interpreter

Status: Independent Contractor

Position Overview:

The Pohnpeian Telephone Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Pohnpeianand English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.

The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.

This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The Interpreters translate verbally.

**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment.**

Essential Job Functions

  • Respond to the interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.
  • **Some calls may be highly emotional and/or stressful in nature. The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes. The interpreter must have the ability to provide the required, company standards of service within this dynamic environment. **

The Crown Is Yours

As a Senior Product Manager, you’ll shape how DraftKings resolves risk cases while building smarter ways to prevent them from happening in the first place. You’ll lead the strategy and roadmap for risk case resolution, using automation, artificial intelligence, and customer self-service to scale our approach as we enter new markets and expand our offerings.   • Partner closely with Risk Operations to understand how cases are worked, identify where agent time is spent, and use case volume, handle time, and other operational data to prioritize opportunities with the greatest impact.

jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!

People Strategy & Executive Partnership

  • Partner with the Hospitality Vertical CEO and other members of the Vertical Leadership Team to develop and execute a people strategy aligned with the Vertical's business objectives and long-term priorities.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to the Vertical CEO, other members of the Vertical Leadership Team, and Business Unit leaders on organizational structure, leadership effectiveness, workforce planning, talent decisions, and complex employee matters.
  • Translate Vertical and Business Unit priorities into practical HR initiatives that strengthen organizational capability and support profitable growth.
  • Identify people-related risks and opportunities across the Hospitality Vertical and develop appropriate strategies to address them.
  • Provide leadership, direction, and guidance to HR professionals supporting businesses across the Vertical.

Talent & Succession

  • Lead the Hospitality Vertical's talent management strategy, including talent reviews, succession planning, leadership development, and identification of high-potential talent.
  • Establish consistent approaches for assessing performance, potential, leadership capability, and organizational readiness across Business Units.
  • Partner with the Vertical Leadership Team and Business Unit leaders to build succession pipelines for critical leadership and specialist roles.
  • Support leadership development initiatives and strengthen management capability throughout the Vertical.
  • Facilitate the movement and development of talent across Business Units and the broader Volaris organization where appropriate.

Performance & Compensation

  • Provide strategic leadership for performance management, goal setting, and annual performance review processes across the Hospitality Vertical.
  • Lead Vertical-level merit and compensation planning, including budget development, market benchmarking, and guidance to Business Unit leaders.
  • Partner with leadership on incentive and bonus structures that align employee outcomes with business performance.
  • Promote consistent compensation principles while recognizing differences in business models, geography, talent markets, and organizational maturity.
  • Analyze workforce and compensation data to identify trends and support informed business decisions.

M&A Due Diligence & Integration

  • Lead the HR workstream for Hospitality Vertical acquisitions, including HR due diligence, identification of employment-related risks, and assessment of compensation, benefits, organizational structure, talent, and HR practices.
  • Partner with the Vertical CEO, other members of the Vertical Leadership Team, M&A, Legal, Finance, and Business Unit leadership throughout the acquisition process.
  • Develop and oversee HR integration plans for newly acquired businesses, balancing Volaris and Vertical requirements with the operating independence of acquired companies.
  • Advise leadership on organizational design, retention, leadership continuity, employee communications, and other people considerations associated with acquisitions.
  • Continuously improve HR due diligence and integration processes based on acquisition experience and the evolving needs of the Hospitality Vertical.

Organizational Effectiveness & Change

  • Advise the Vertical CEO, Vertical Leadership Team, and Business Unit leaders on organizational design and ensure structures, roles, and leadership capabilities support business strategy.
  • Lead or support significant organizational changes, including restructurings, leadership transitions, acquisitions, and organizational realignments.
  • Develop practical change and communication strategies that help leaders successfully implement organizational changes.
  • Support Business Units in building scalable people practices as their organizations grow and evolve.


HR Operations, Governance & Risk

  • Establish appropriate HR standards, frameworks, and governance across the Hospitality Vertical while preserving Volaris' decentralized operating philosophy.
  • Ensure Business Units maintain effective HR practices and comply with applicable employment requirements in the jurisdictions in which they operate.
  • Partner with Legal and external advisors on complex employment matters and significant employee relations issues.
  • Provide oversight and guidance related to HR systems, policies, benefits, payroll, and other HR operational processes where Vertical-level coordination creates value.
  • Use workforce analytics and HR metrics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities and provide meaningful insights to the Vertical CEO and Vertical Leadership Team.

Desired Training and Education:

jobs.title: Account Manager
jobs.excerpt: Dispatch is redefining how the world experiences home and field service.
jobs.description:
Dispatch is redefining how the world experiences home and field service. Founded in 2013 and trusted by leading brands and service providers, we power seamless, reliable service experiences through a modern platform built for scale. Our platform gives businesses the visibility, communication, and control they need to manage every step of the service journey, from job acceptance through completion.

As part of Manos Software, a Valsoft operating group, Dispatch combines the focus and agility of a specialized software company with the long-term support of a global vertical SaaS organization. We’re investing in our product, our customers, and our team with a focus on sustainable growth.

THE ROLE

Our Customer Success team owns the long-term relationship with Dispatch’s enterprise customers and their service provider networks. As an Account Manager, you will be accountable for two things across a portfolio of strategic accounts: keeping our customers, and growing them. You will own retention, renewal, upsell, and cross-sell from the first conversation to signed contract - and you will carry a target for net revenue growth within your book.

You won’t get there by working a ticket queue. You’ll earn it by knowing each customer’s business as well as they do: how they make money, how their service operations run, which metrics their leadership watches, and where they are headed next. You will act as a trusted consultant, bringing ideas and best practices that improve their service operations. Once you understand the business that well, growth follows. You will spot where Dispatch’s newest products and capabilities fit, and you’ll bring those opportunities to the customer and help turn them into expansion.

AS THE ACCOUNT MANAGER YOU WILL:

Protect and Renew the Base

  • Own gross and net retention for your book of enterprise accounts, driving on-time renewals with no surprises
  • Monitor account health through adoption, usage, program performance, and stakeholder sentiment, and step in early when risk signals appear
  • Build and execute account plans that tie the Dispatch program to each customer’s business goals and secure long-term renewal
  • Serve as the escalation point for critical issues, rallying internal teams to resolve them and rebuild confidence

Build Deep, Multi-Level Relationships

  • Develop trusted relationships from day-to-day users and program champions up to the executive sponsors and decision makers in operations, finance, and IT
  • Avoid single-threaded accounts by building a network of advocates in every customer and across their service provider networks
  • Set a consistent communication cadence and lead Executive Business Reviews that focus on outcomes, not activity
  • Develop references, referrals, and customer advocates who will speak on Dispatch’s behalf

Know the Customer’s Business and Consult

  • Learn each customer’s business model, service operations, competitive pressures, and strategic priorities in depth
  • Act as a consultant: diagnose operational challenges, recommend workflow and process improvements, and share field service best practices
  • Build and present value and ROI stories that connect Dispatch to the customer’s KPIs, such as first-time completion, speed to service, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve
  • Bring the voice of the customer to the Dispatch Product team and help shape the roadmap around real business needs

Grow Accounts with New Products

  • Find expansion opportunities by matching new Dispatch products and capabilities to each customer’s gaps and goals
  • Stay current on product releases and turn them into clear, customer-specific value propositions
  • Own the full commercial cycle for your accounts: prospect within the base, qualify, propose, negotiate, and close upsell and cross-sell deals yourself
  • Expand Dispatch’s footprint within each account: new business units, regions, service lines, and service provider networks
  • Build a growth plan for every account that maps current usage against the full Dispatch portfolio, and prioritize the biggest whitespace opportunities
  • Uncover new budget and buying centers by building relationships beyond your core champion, in areas such as operations, customer experience, claims, and finance
  • Use adoption, performance, and ROI data to build the business case for expansion, so each upsell is presented as a clear return for the customer
  • Lead new product pilots and proofs of value with existing customers, then turn successful results into broader rollouts
  • Use renewals as a chance to grow: combine renewals with expansions, multi-year commitments, and pricing that reflects the value delivered
  • Own and forecast your expansion pipeline in Salesforce with accuracy, and hit quarterly net revenue retention and expansion targets

Requirements

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

  • 5+ years in Customer Success or Account Management at a SaaS or high-technology company, working with large enterprise accounts
  • Consulting or Professional Services experience strongly preferred, and comfort diagnosing a customer’s business and recommending a path forward
  • Experience managing multiple $250K+ ARR accounts with ownership of renewal and retention targets
  • A proven record of high gross and net retention, including saving at-risk accounts and closing complex renewals
  • A track record of growing accounts through upsell, cross-sell, and the adoption of new products, with experience carrying an expansion or net revenue retention target
  • Experience owning the full sales cycle with existing customers, from building the business case to negotiating pricing and closing the deal, without handing off to a sales team
  • The business acumen to understand how a customer makes money and to speak credibly about operations, P&L impact, and ROI
  • Confidence presenting to, working with, and advising senior leaders at Fortune 1000 companies
  • Enough technical savvy to have a working knowledge of how software gets built
  • A self-starter who drives accounts proactively with minimal oversight and thrives in a fast-paced, results-driven culture
  • Field service, home services, insurance, warranty, or service-network experience is a strong plus

SKILLS WE SEEK:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, presentation, and facilitation skills
  • A consultative, curious approach: you ask great questions and listen more than you talk
  • Strong relationship-building, negotiation, and executive presence
  • Analytical ability to turn usage and performance data into insights and recommendations
  • Strong leadership, teamwork, and cross-functional collaboration skills
  • Project management skills: the ability to coordinate competing tasks and manage multiple priorities
  • Keen attention to detail and adherence to deadlines
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, etc.)
  • Knowledge of basic SQL and Customer Success technology (Salesforce, Pendo, etc.)

WITHIN ONE MONTH, YOU WILL:

  • Attend Dispatch’s New Hire Orientation
  • Meet one-on-one with Customer Success leadership, Product, and Support to learn what’s working, what isn’t, and where the biggest opportunities are
  • Gain a strong understanding of the field service industry, the business challenges Dispatch solves, and the full Dispatch product suite, including new offerings
  • Review each of your accounts: health, renewal dates, key stakeholders, and known risks

WITHIN THREE MONTHS, YOU WILL:

  • Know your customers’ businesses well enough to start teaching us something we don’t know
  • Own day-to-day relationships and a regular communication cadence across all of your accounts
  • Have a documented account plan for each customer covering business goals, stakeholder map, health, renewal strategy, and growth opportunities
  • Own your renewal targets and have mitigation plans in place for any at-risk accounts
  • Complete a whitespace analysis across your book and identify your first expansion opportunities for new products
  • Build, own, and report on a qualified expansion pipeline for your book

WITHIN SIX MONTHS, YOU WILL:

  • Have executive-level relationships in each of your key accounts
  • Coordinate and lead Executive Business Reviews that show measurable value and ROI
  • Be seen by your customers as a strategic advisor, not only a point of contact
  • Close renewals on time and close your first expansion deals
  • Launch at least one new product pilot or proof of value with an existing customer

WITHIN TWELVE MONTHS, YOU WILL:

  • Consistently achieve or exceed your gross retention, net retention, and expansion targets
  • Lead value-planning discussions with customers backed by adoption, program performance, and ROI metrics
  • Have measurably increased the ARR in your book through new products, business units, or service provider networks
  • Have turned successful pilots into full rollouts and have customer case studies that support future growth
  • Be an expert in software solutions for field service, with a wide network of relationships across the industry

Benefits

SALARY

The base salary range for this role is between $90,000 - $110,000 annually. Actual pay within the range is influenced by multiple factors, including but not limited to skill set, your residence location, and prior work experience. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for benefits and bonus, which are not included in the provided pay range.

LOCATION

Dispatch fully accommodates remote work, as long as you have a permanent residence in Canada or the many US states we are registered in. Want to spend a month in Italy? Great, do it! Live in Maine? Sweet, we have another team member there! As long as you are crushing your goals and helping us drive the business forward, you do you. We also have an office in Boston that is open and available for you to use.

WE HAVE

  • An amazing team focused on innovating and improving every day
  • Room for growth and an emphasis on talent development including a professional development reimbursement program
  • A fun, casual team environment with co-workers who will make you feel like you are an important part of our team, engage you in developing new solutions to challenging problems, and help you leverage your strengths
  • A generous medical, dental, and vision package with 90% covered by us!
  • Paid parental leave
  • 401k with company match
  • Company sponsored Life Insurance coverage, short term disability, long term disability
  • Additional perks including a wellness and adventure fund, as well as monthly personal Uber credits
  • Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO), 9 company Holidays, and a flexible work schedule

Still with us?

We’re ready to meet you if you wake up every day eager to get your hands dirty in a high growth start-up atmosphere. Is this role not an exact fit for you? Keep an eye on our Careers Page for other positions!

jobs.description:
CrossCountry Mortgage (CCM) is the nation's number one distributed retail mortgage lender with more than 9,000 employees operating over 700 branches and servicing loans across all 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico. Our company has been recognized ten times on the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private businesses and has received many awards for our standout culture.

A culture where you can grow! CCM has created an exceptional culture driving employee engagement, exceeding employee expectations, and directly impacting company success. At our core, our entrepreneurial spirit empowers every employee to be who they are to help us move forward together. You’ll get unwavering support from all departments and total transparency from the top down.

CCM offers eligible employees a competitive compensation plan and a robust benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, as well as a 401K. We also offer company-provided short-term disability, an employee assistance program, and a wellness program.

Position Overview:

The Director, Compliance provides strategic oversight of the Company’s post-closing suspense and compliance issue management functions. This role establishes and maintains a risk-based framework for identifying, assessing, escalating, remediating, and resolving post-closing deficiencies, compliance exceptions, system deficiencies, and regulatory issues. Through centralized governance, executive reporting, and cross-functional oversight, the Director, Compliance strengthens the Compliance Management System (CMS) and promotes a culture of compliance and regulatory excellence.


Job Responsibilities:


  • Oversee the end-to-end post-closing suspense function, including intake, assignment, aging, prioritization, escalation, and remediation, ensuring adherence to regulatory and investor requirements.
  • Conduct in-file reviews to draft responses and/or rebuttals to Compliance PCQC findings.
  • Establish governance and escalation protocols for aged, overdue, or unresolved post-closing suspense items.
  • Analyze post-closing suspense trends to identify systemic, recurring, or material deficiencies requiring formal issue escalation, root-cause analysis, corrective action, or broader remediation.
  • Build and execute periodic diagnostic testing for suspected emerging risks.
  • Govern the compliance issue lifecycle from identification through closure, including issue classification and risk rating, root-cause analysis, accountable ownership, target completion dates, escalation of overdue or materially deficient remediation, validation of corrective actions, and formal closure.
  • Act as the critical point-of-contact for wide-spread/systemic issues, working with key stakeholders to identify the root cause of the issue, stopping the issue from impacting additional transactions, remedying impacted transactions, creating controls to detect/prevent future recurrences, establishing ongoing monitoring of the issue, and thoroughly documenting the issue and its resolution.
  • Facilitate the corrective action lifecycle, including root cause analysis, control implementation, and post-implementation validation testing for issues identified through examinations, monitoring & testing, Post-Closing Quality Control, and Internal Audit.
  • Drive continuous improvement in post-closing compliance processes through technology adoption, workflow automation, and data analytics, leveraging emerging tools to increase throughput, accuracy, and auditability.
  • Develop and maintain a centralized issue management repository and reporting dashboards that promote transparency and provide timely visibility into issue status, aging, risk ratings, remediation progress, and resolution activities.
  • Partner with Regulatory Change Management to identify regulatory developments that may affect post-closing controls, generate compliance issues, or require proactive remediation.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness and sustainability of remediation actions through rigorous post-closure testing and validation, ensuring issues do not recur and that systemic weaknesses are addressed holistically.
  • Produce executive-level compliance reporting that provides senior and executive leadership with clear, timely, and actionable insights into issue aging, emerging trends, key risk indicators, remediation progress, and the effectiveness and sustainability of corrective actions.
  • Coordinate issue responses and supporting materials for regulatory examinations, internal audits, investor reviews, and other oversight activities.
  • Fulfill additional responsibilities and special projects as assigned.

Qualifications and Skills:


  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 7+ years of experience within a financial institution, preferably a large or complex organization.
  • 5+ years of experience in risk management or consumer compliance, specifically related to mortgage originations.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in managing compliance issues, corrective action plans, post-closing deficiencies, root-cause analysis, remediation, and issue validation within a mortgage lending environment.
  • Advanced working knowledge of mortgage lending and compliance processes, as well as enterprise workflow platforms, including Encompass, Mavent, Jira, and Salesforce, preferred.
  • Comprehensive understanding of mortgage loan operations and associated control frameworks across the origination lifecycle.
  • Advanced knowledge of federal and state mortgage lending regulations, including but not limited to the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, QM/ATR, RESPA, TILA, TRID, ECOA, HMDA, GLBA, Fair Lending, UDAAP, and SAFE Act.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills to convey complex information clearly and effectively.
  • Advanced prioritization and time management skills to effectively manage competing priorities and meet critical deadlines.

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

About Sentient:

Sentient is the only nonprofit, nonpartisan news organization solely focused on factory farms and their effects on climate, animals, workers, clean water, public health and rural communities. Founded in 2018, Sentient’s content is fact-checked and science-driven, with reporting that serves readers—especially those in frontline rural communities—interested in the impacts of what they eat on animals, climate, water, workers and their local economy.

Position Overview:

Sentient is seeking an experienced Managing Editor to help lead our growing newsroom and oversee the day-to-day editorial operations behind our investigative and accountability journalism on factory farming and its effects on climate, animals, workers, public health and rural communities.
Reporting to Sentient’s Editor-in-Chief, the Managing Editor will manage daily editorial workflow, work closely with editors, staff reporters and freelance contributors, oversee story assignments and edits, and help set and uphold Sentient’s editorial standards across the newsroom.
This role is central to ensuring Sentient’s journalism is accurate, timely and impactful, and will play a key part in managing the newsroom’s continued growth.

Key Responsibilities:

Editorial Management

  • Oversee day-to-day editorial operations and manage the daily production workflow across staff reporters, editors and freelance contributors.

  • Manage a number of editorial staff members, including editors, production coordinator and reporters.

  • Partner with the Editor-in-Chief to set and maintain editorial standards, style guidelines and fact-checking practices across the newsroom.

  • Manage editorial calendars and coverage plans, balancing daily coverage with longer investigative projects.

  • As needed, edit and shape stories for accuracy, clarity, fairness and impact, from pitch through publication.

  • Help recruit, onboard and manage freelance contributors.

  • Ensure all published work aligns with Sentient’s editorial mission and standards for accuracy, nuance and journalistic rigor.

Newsroom Leadership

  • Work closely with the Editor-in-Chief on overall editorial strategy and coverage priorities.

  • Help manage editorial budgets, including freelance spending.

  • Support hiring, training and performance feedback for editorial staff.

  • Represent Sentient’s editorial standards in collaborations with partner newsrooms and outlets.

  • Track and report on editorial output, deadlines and story performance.

  • Step in for the Editor-in-Chief on editorial decisions as needed.

Cross-Team Collaboration

  • Collaborate with the social media, audience and video teams to adapt and distribute reporting across platforms.

  • Work with the development team to support grant reporting and impact tracking related to editorial output.

  • Partner with reporters on regional projects, such as the Iowa Reporting Project, to ensure consistent editorial standards.

Requirements

  • Significant experience in journalism, including several years in a newsroom manager or leadership role.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple reporters, projects and deadlines simultaneously.

  • Strong news judgment and a track record of shaping accurate, high-impact journalism.

  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.

  • Experience with fact-checking and editorial standards processes.

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fully remote environment.

Highly Desired Qualifications

  • Experience reporting or editing on agriculture, food systems, climate, animal welfare or environmental issues.

  • Experience managing freelance writers and contributors.

  • Experience in nonprofit or mission-driven journalism.

  • Familiarity with audience engagement.

  • Experience with data journalism or investigative reporting techniques.

The Recruitment Process
We want to provide transparency around the recruitment process so you can know what to expect when applying. We are looking to select a candidate for the Managing Editor role over the coming months and want to allow sufficient time for candidates to apply and for us to assess those who have applied.
The recruitment process is expected to proceed as follows:

  • Step 1: Submit your application at the link below and we will review your application. Please include a resume and a cover letter.

  • Step 2: Candidates who pass the initial screening round will be invited to a first-round interview with our hiring team.

  • Step 3: Candidates who pass the first-round interview stage can expect a second interview stage with a time-limited work test for which we will compensate candidates for their time.

  • Step 4: Candidates who have been successful in the second interview stage and time-limited work test will be invited to a third interview round with Sentient’s leadership team.

We appreciate your interest in Sentient and even if you are unsuccessful in applying for this position, we invite you to apply to work with us again in the future. We do think it is important to share that we are a small non-profit news outlet, and due to the volume of applicants, it may not be possible for us to respond to everyone who has applied during the first step of the process.

Benefits

This is a full-time (40 hours per week) position that is remote. We are looking for candidates that are compatible with Eastern Time Zone working hours.
Our total reward offering for this position includes the following:

  • Salary: $110,000 - $118,000 USD annually.

  • Health, Dental & Vision Benefits.

  • Professional Development Allowance.

  • 401K plan.

  • Competitive Paid Time Off.

  • Annual Remote Office Supply Stipend

Equity and Inclusion StatementSentient is committed to building an inclusive and equitable newsroom that reflects the diversity of the communities we cover. We believe that journalism should amplify the voices of those most affected by industrial animal agriculture, particularly those from historically marginalized groups. We encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to people of color, women, LGBTQ+ individuals, people with disabilities and those from rural or economically disadvantaged communities. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Romania Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-80,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Bilingual Patient Follow-Up Specialist

Remote | Personal Injury | Part-Time, 30 hours/week initially | $6.5/hour

About the Role

We are seeking a highly organized, dependable, and personable Bilingual Patient Follow-Up Specialist to support a growing personal injury medical practice.

The immediate priority for this role is addressing a significant backlog of patient follow-up calls. You will conduct outbound outreach, document patient recovery progress, support attorney and legal documentation requests, and help ensure that tasks are completed accurately and on time.

The ideal candidate combines strong medical assistant experience with excellent communication, persistence, accuracy, and the ability to handle sensitive patient and legal information with a very high level of attention to detail.

Key Responsibilities

Patient Follow-Up & Outreach

  • Contact patients approximately 4 to 6 weeks after their visit to check on their recovery and current condition.

  • Conduct consistent outbound outreach through calls, texts, or other approved channels while remaining professional and respectful.

  • Follow up persistently when patients are difficult to reach without becoming overly aggressive or pushy.

Symptom Tracking & Documentation

  • Complete structured follow-up questionnaires regarding symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, and other reported concerns.

  • Record patient responses accurately in the practice's dedicated symptom tracking database.

  • Maintain complete and organized documentation so the physician can easily review patient recovery progress.

Legal Records & Billing Requests

  • Respond to requests from attorneys and law firms for patient evaluations, medical records, and billing documentation.

  • Compile the correct records and ensure all requested information is complete before sending or uploading it.

  • Handle legal and medical documentation with extremely high accuracy because errors can directly affect personal injury cases.

Portal & Task Management

  • Upload completed evaluations, records, bills, and other requested documentation into designated attorney or client portals.

  • Track outstanding requests and completed tasks so documentation does not fall through the cracks.

  • Maintain organized records across the clinic's internal systems and external portals.

Reporting & Operational Reliability

  • Provide End-of-Day reports summarizing completed calls, outreach attempts, pending follow-ups, and finished tasks.

  • Maintain consistent follow-through on assigned responsibilities and communicate quickly when an issue could affect completion.

  • Prioritize accuracy and reliability, particularly when handling patient records, legal requests, and time-sensitive documentation.

Cross-Training & Practice Support

  • Learn the Scheduling & Intake Specialist's core workflows, including scheduling, patient intake, and patient communication.

  • Provide backup coverage when the other VMA is unavailable or when patient volume increases.

  • Assist with incoming calls, emails, patient questions, or administrative work when additional practice support is required.

Required Qualifications

  • Fully fluent in English and Spanish.

  • Previous experience as a Medical Assistant, Medical Receptionist, Virtual Medical Assistant, or similar healthcare support professional.

  • Strong understanding of medical terminology and patient communication.

  • Exceptional attention to detail when entering records or managing documentation.

  • Strong telephone communication skills with a warm, conversational, and patient-centered approach.

  • Comfortable performing frequent outbound patient calls and follow-ups.

  • Highly organized and capable of independently tracking multiple open tasks.

  • Able to work consistently during Mountain Time business hours.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience working with personal injury practices.

  • Experience communicating with attorneys or law firms.

  • Experience fulfilling medical records or billing documentation requests.

  • Familiarity with legal, clinic, or attorney portals.

Tools & Systems

  • Internal Clinic Symptom Database for documenting standardized patient follow-up responses and recovery symptoms.

  • External Law Firm/Clinic Portals for uploading completed evaluations, medical records, bills, and other requested documentation.

  • GoLean Productivity Tool and GoLean Private Network for productivity monitoring and secure access to practice systems and patient information.

What Success Looks Like

  • The existing patient follow-up backlog is steadily cleared, with patients contacted approximately 4 to 6 weeks after their visit and their recovery information documented accurately.

  • Attorney and law firm requests for evaluations, medical records, and billing documentation are completed accurately and on time, with the practice expecting effectively zero preventable errors.

  • Follow-ups, portal uploads, records requests, and outstanding tasks are consistently tracked through completion, with clear End-of-Day reporting and reliable backup coverage for scheduling and intake when needed.

Overview

You will define technical strategy, drive cross-functional alignment, and own systems that directly shape payment accuracy, risk adjustment, and quality outcomes for the payers we serve. This role sits at the intersection of applied research and production engineering, translating ambiguous, high-stakes problems into scalable, auditable ML solutions.

The ideal candidate has operated at large scope across multiple teams and product surfaces — not just shipped models, but defined the problem, built the evaluation infrastructure, created the data flywheel, and drove measurable business outcomes. They think in systems, write crisp design docs, bring intellectual honesty to experimentation, and treat auditability and precision as first-class requirements rather than afterthoughts. They raise the level of the engineers around them.

Responsibilities

  • Drive the data flywheel: convert expert clinician and auditor review decisions into high-quality labeled data, and close the loop with fine-tuning of models to lift detection precision.

  • Lead ranking and prioritization systems that surface the highest-value claims, audits, and care gaps for human review, improving both reviewer efficiency and financial impact.

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Refer them!
